items.description: D6 (and A11, the Risks table, and O4) treat `--network slirp4netns:allow_host_loopback=false` as proof that host services are unreachable from PR code. That option only disables the 10.0.2.2 -> 127.0.0.1 mapping. slirp4netns still NATs container traffic through the host stack, so any host service bound to 0.0.0.0 or to the host's LAN/Tailscale address (a compose-published Postgres `0.0.0.0:54322` is the common case, and the ri-08 dispatcher daemon may also listen non-loopback) remains reachable by connecting to the host's real IP. The O4 verification (`curl http://10.0.2.2:54322`) would pass while Postgres is reachable at `http://<host-lan-ip>:54322`, so the isolation claim is unverified by the test the runbook prescribes. Fix: (a) state the binding assumption explicitly in D6/A11 (host services must bind to 127.0.0.1 only, verified in O4 with `ss -ltnp` for :54322 and the coordinator port); (b) extend the O4 check to `curl` the host's primary address (`hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'`) from inside the container; (c) optionally add a host nftables/ufw rule in O1 that drops `owner uid ghrunner` OUTPUT traffic to the host's own addresses, which is the only control that holds regardless of how services are bound.

A10 and D6 argue that every same-repository branch author is a trusted human principal. This repository explicitly accepts PRs from automated authors with push access (Dependabot, Jules, Codex and other agent PRs, per the merge-pull-requests skill and the `dependency-update-remediation` job). Their branches satisfy `head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, so with `CI_RUNNER_LANE=self-hosted` unreviewed agent-generated code and freshly bumped third-party packages execute on the GX10 host (shared kernel, shared uv cache that later `main` jobs read) before any human has looked at the diff. The hardening in D6 is good, but the written trust argument is wrong as stated, and the acceptance of the cache-poisoning risk rests on it. This is a threat-model call for the owner: either extend A10 to name automated same-repo authors and accept it, or add `github.actor` / branch-prefix exclusions (e.g. `dependabot/*`, bot actors) to the D3 expression so those PRs stay on hosted runners.

Re-verification of open ledger items #3 and #16: still open. (1) The MUST that the `fromJSON` label set equals `routing.self_hosted_labels` has no scenario (the 'JIT labels' scenario is about the mint script), and nothing ties `vars.CI_RUNNER_LANE` / `inputs.runner_lane` in the expression to `routing.repository_variable` / `routing.dispatch_input`. (2) 'The CLI SHALL select runs only through explicit filters … and SHALL cap fetched runs with `--limit`' still has no WHEN/THEN; task 4.1 checks argument parsing only, which would not detect a client that paginates everything before truncating. Add one scenario for each clause (for #2: with a stubbed `gh` returning N pages, at most ceil(limit/per_page) requests are issued).

O1 creates `ghrunner` with `useradd --system`. On Ubuntu, system accounts receive no `/etc/subuid` / `/etc/subgid` range, and rootless podman cannot run an image whose process user is non-root (the actions-runner image runs as `runner`, uid 1001) without one: O3 (`podman build`) and O4 (`podman run`) fail with a 'no subuid ranges found' class error. Also, `--shell /usr/sbin/nologin` means the 'as `ghrunner`' instructions in O3/O4 cannot be followed via `su`/`machinectl shell`; the runbook should say `sudo -u ghrunner XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u ghrunner) ...` or `systemd-run --user --machine=ghrunner@`.

The design uses 'the env file' for two different files: the operator configuration (`gx10-runner.env.example`: repo slug, limits, image ref, labels, `GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED`) and the per-instance container env file written by the mint script (`%t/gx10-runner/%i.env`, JIT config and runner id only). D7's property list never names the `EnvironmentFile=` line that must load the former, nor how the credential reaches the unit (`LoadCredential=github-token:<path>` vs `GX10_RUNNER_TOKEN_FILE`), and test 3.1 does not assert either. Relatedly, 'GX10_RUNNER_UV_CACHE=off drops the volume' is not expressible in a plain `ExecStart=` line; it needs an unquoted `$GX10_UV_CACHE_ARGS` word-split variable or a wrapper, and either choice interacts with the test that scans `ExecStart` for a literal volume flag.

Re-verification of open ledger item #6: still open. The D6 option list has `--name gx10-runner-%i` without `--replace`, so after any unclean stop (podman client killed at `TimeoutStopSec`, host crash) the stale container name makes every subsequent `ExecStart` fail and `Restart=always` spins every 10 s with the instance silently out of the pool. Add `--replace` to the required options (and to test 3.1), and have `mint-jitconfig.sh` or `cleanup-runner.sh` sweep offline registrations matching `gx10-<hostname>-<instance>-*` before minting, since `ExecStopPost` never runs on power loss (O10).

The session log records the shared uv cache as 'the main source of speedup' for outcome 2, but nothing in D6/D10 ensures routed jobs actually use the mounted path. If the workflows use `astral-sh/setup-uv` with its default caching (the design does not say), the action exports `UV_CACHE_DIR` under `$RUNNER_TEMP` and round-trips the cache through GitHub's cache service, bypassing `/home/runner/.cache/uv` entirely; the volume would then be dead weight and the A6 threshold would be measured against a cold cache. The design should state the binding: set `UV_CACHE_DIR=/home/runner/.cache/uv` in the container image/env, and either set `cache-local-path` to it or `enable-cache: false` when `runner.environment == 'self-hosted'`.

Stale or duplicated text left by the iteration edits: (1) D6 repeats the 'operator can disable the cache with GX10_RUNNER_UV_CACHE=off' paragraph twice in succession; (2) session-log.md PLAN section still says 'assumptions A1-A9' and its trade-off entry still claims 'locked hash verification applies', which plan-findings #4 and A10 explicitly retract; (3) spec signatures `median_wallclock(runs)` / `compare(baseline, candidate, threshold=0.85, min_n=5)` differ from design D8's keyword-only forms with a `conclusion` parameter.

Re-verification of open ledger item #9: still open, text unchanged. `ACTIONS_RUNNER_INPUT_JITCONFIG` stays in every step's environment and carries the runner's key material; PR code can act as that runner against the Actions broker for the job's lifetime. Replace 'gains nothing' with an explicit residual-risk statement bounded by ephemerality, optionally noting the `unset`-and-pass-`--jitconfig` entrypoint wrapper as a hardening follow-up.

Design D3 excludes fork code only when `github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. A `merge_group` run can execute a temporary merge commit containing an approved fork PR, but the expression treats every `merge_group` as non-fork and routes it to GX10 whenever `CI_RUNNER_LANE=self-hosted`. This violates the requirement that fork code never execute on self-hosted runners. Route all `merge_group` runs to hosted runners unless fork provenance can be established safely.

D8 requires `verify_run` to correlate manifest job IDs with jobs returned by GitHub's workflow-jobs API, but that API exposes display names rather than stable YAML job IDs; matrix jobs can also produce multiple names from one job definition. No mapping or naming contract is defined, so missing-job, lane, conditional-skip, and hosted/routed checks cannot be implemented reliably. Define and test a stable correlation mechanism, including matrix expansions.

Assumption A10 equates the ability to create a same-repository branch with authorization to persist code into later trusted runs through the shared uv cache. That premise ignores Dependabot and other automation, compromised collaborator credentials, and branch-protection distinctions between pushing a branch and merging to protected main. A PR can poison the writable cache and influence a later main job with stronger credentials. Disable cross-trust cache sharing or isolate caches by trust level; otherwise require explicit human risk acceptance.

Operator step O11 invokes `verify-run` without `--expect-lane hosted`, although `verify-run` defaults to `self-hosted`. A correctly routed fork PR would therefore report every routed job on GitHub-hosted runners as a violation instead of producing the stated zero-violation result. O11 and its runbook command must pass `--expect-lane hosted`.

D6 promises that `GX10_RUNNER_UV_CACHE=off` removes the cache volume, but neither the systemd-unit contract nor tasks 3.1–3.2 define or test how that switch changes `ExecStart`. An implementation can satisfy the planned tests while always mounting the cache or passing the literal value `off` to Podman. Specify the argument-expansion or wrapper mechanism and add positive tests for both enabled and disabled modes.

The artifacts disagree on failed `continue-on-error` jobs. Design D8 and task 4.1 require them to be warnings, while the specification says `verify_run` SHALL report every conclusion other than `success` or `skipped`, and the CLI exits nonzero on every violation. Define the result model and exit behavior explicitly and add a WHEN/THEN scenario for the warning exception.

The specification's normative CLI clause requiring explicit run filters and a bounded `--limit` has no WHEN/THEN scenario that verifies filtering or bounded pagination. Task 4.1 only checks argument parsing, which would not detect an implementation that fetches all pages before truncating. Add a scenario covering request selection and the maximum number of fetched results/pages.

work-packages.yaml contracts.openapi.primary and files reference openspec/changes/migrate-ci-to-self-hosted-gx10-runners/... paths directly. Per OpenSpec path stability guide (docs/guides/openspec-path-stability.md), these paths are unstable — archival moves them to openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<id>/. Any tooling consuming work-packages.yaml for contract resolution may break post-archive. The package verification commands correctly use promoted .github/ paths.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: repo convention: change-local contract paths in work-packages are consumed pre-archive; path-stability rule targets tests

items.description: spec.md lacks an explicit SHALL requirement that both workflows MUST declare a workflow_dispatch trigger with runner_lane choice input (auto | hosted | self-hosted). Multiple scenarios (e.g., 'Dispatch input overrides the variable in both directions', 'Unset variable keeps CI on hosted runners') reference workflow_dispatch events and the runner_lane input, but no requirement mandates the trigger's existence. Tasks.md 2.7 and design.md D3 implement it.

spec.md 'Requirement: Runners Are Ephemeral Per Job' lists 7 SHALL statements but omits the cleanup-runner.sh ExecStopPost requirement. The scenario 'Unit runs a removable container with a single-use config' checks that ExecStopPost invokes cleanup-runner.sh, but the requirement text should include it for completeness.

spec.md 'Requirement: Runners Survive Host Reboot Via systemd' does not explicitly require the install-units.sh script to be copy-and-print-only (non-mutating during tests). The scenario 'Install script does not mutate the host during tests' covers this behavior, but the requirement text should mandate it.

spec.md does not document the known limit that the tool-parity static scan only examines run: blocks and cannot detect container-engine commands invoked indirectly through scripts (e.g., run_live_matrix.sh calling podman). Design.md D10 explicitly documents this limit and the O6 dry-run backstop. The spec should include a scenario or note acknowledging this limitation.

runner-lanes.schema.json allows arbitrary self_hosted_labels array (minItems: 2, uniqueItems: true, contains: 'self-hosted') but the canonical D3 runs-on expression hardcodes fromJSON('["self-hosted","linux","ARM64","gx10"]'). The schema should constrain self_hosted_labels to exactly these 4 labels (or at minimum enforce the exact array) to prevent drift between manifest and expression. The spec scenario 'JIT labels match the routing labels' tests equality but the schema permits divergence.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: drift is caught by tests 2.1/3.3 tying expression and mint labels to the manifest; schema stays reusable

items.description: wp-runner-kit package outputs.artifacts list omits gx10-runner.env.example, which is authored in task 3.2, referenced in design.md D7, and required for operator configuration. The artifact should be listed for completeness.

work-packages.yaml contracts.openapi.primary points to a README.md file instead of an OpenAPI spec. The comment acknowledges 'The schema requires an openapi block, so primary points at the README that records that decision.' This workaround may cause tooling that expects a valid OpenAPI document to fail or misbehave.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: repo convention for changes with no HTTP surface (recorded in contracts/README.md)

items.description: proposal.md assumptions list has inconsistent formatting: A1-A9 use '- **A1.**' format with no blank lines between entries, but a blank line separates A9 from A10/A11, making them appear as a separate list. Minor readability issue.

loop-state.json records two degradations: 'coordinator_projection_forbidden' (project-state submit returned forbidden) and 'audit_sink_failed' (audit sink reported failure for gate proposal_approval decision auto). These are infrastructure issues in the coordinator environment, not plan defects, but should be monitored as they may affect subsequent phases.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: environment degradations, not plan defects

items.description: The preferred host-isolation control in D6 (`meta skuid ghrunner fib daddr type local drop`, repeated in A11, tasks O4 and the spec scenario 'Operator verifies host services are unreachable on every host address') drops every packet owned by uid ghrunner whose destination is a local address. On an Ubuntu 24.04 host the resolver is systemd-resolved's stub at 127.0.0.53, which is a local address, so the rule also drops (a) the mint script's own DNS lookups for api.github.com — `ExecStartPre` then burns its whole `GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED` budget on every start and no instance ever comes online — and (b) slirp4netns's forwarding of container DNS (10.0.2.3) to the host resolver, so even a minted runner cannot resolve github.com. The rule as written wedges the entire pool and the spec scenario would literally pass (the rule 'is listed'). Fix: exempt the resolver (`meta skuid ghrunner ip daddr 127.0.0.53 udp dport 53 accept` and the tcp equivalent, placed before the drop), or point the containers at a non-local resolver with `--dns` and state that the mint script's resolver must not be loopback; add that exemption to O4's listed rule and to the spec scenario's AND clause.

The O4 isolation probe uses `curl http://<addr>:<port> && echo reachable || echo unreachable`. Against Postgres on :54322 the TCP connect succeeds, Postgres rejects the HTTP bytes and closes, and curl exits non-zero (52 'Empty reply' or 56 'Recv failure'), so the probe prints `unreachable` precisely when the port IS reachable. The same false negative applies to any non-HTTP service. Since the design (D6) makes this probe the required evidence that the nftables/loopback control holds, the runbook would certify isolation that does not exist. Use a transport-level check (`bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/<addr>/<port>'`, `nc -z -w3`, or treat only curl exit codes 7 and 28 as 'unreachable') and reword the spec scenario 'every probe fails' to 'every TCP connect is refused or times out'.

D6 (the ledger-#7 fix) now requires two concrete artefacts — the image sets `UV_CACHE_DIR=/home/runner/.cache/uv`, and routed jobs that use `astral-sh/setup-uv` pass `cache-local-path: /home/runner/.cache/uv` — but nothing implements or tests them: tasks 2.5–2.8 (workflow edits), 3.6/3.7 (Containerfile and its test) and the wp-workflows / wp-runner-kit package descriptions do not mention either, and no spec scenario covers them. The measured A6 speedup when the operator opts in would silently be against a bypassed cache. Add the `ENV UV_CACHE_DIR` line to task 3.7 (asserted in test 3.6), add the setup-uv `cache-local-path` edit to task 2.8 (asserted in test_tool_parity or test_routing_expression for routed jobs), and note that on the hosted lane the path is harmless because ubuntu-latest's user is also `runner`.

The D8 correlation contract makes `verify_run` depend on the workflow definition (job-level `if:`, literal `name:`, `strategy.matrix`, `continue-on-error`), yet (a) wp-tooling's scope lists `.github/workflows/**` under `deny` and omits it from `read_allow`, so the implementer cannot build fixtures from the live workflows; and (b) neither D8 nor task 4.3 says where the CLI obtains the definition — reading the local checkout while verifying a run from another commit (O6 on `main`, O11 on a fork PR) misattributes `if:`/names after any workflow edit. State that `verify-run` fetches `.github/workflows/<file>` at the run's `head_sha` via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/...?ref=<sha>` (read-only, within the boundary) or takes `--workflow-file`, and widen wp-tooling's read scope.

The ledger-#12/#14 fix renamed the switch to `GX10_RUNNER_CACHE_ARGS` and inverted the default (cache off), but the companion documents were not updated: session-log.md's PLAN trade-off still says the cache is on, 'locked hash verification applies' and names `GX10_RUNNER_UV_CACHE=off`; its PLAN_ITERATE section still records 'Accept shared uv cache in solo mode as A10'; its Relevant Files line still says 'assumptions A1-A9'; plan-findings.md #4 still says team mode 'requires GX10_RUNNER_UV_CACHE=off'; and proposal.md § What Changes item 4 still says verify-run checks 'every job succeeded', contradicting D8's skipped/warning rules. A reader following the session log will look for a variable that no longer exists.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: proposal What-Changes item 4 fixed; session-log.md and plan-findings.md are historical phase records and are not rewritten

items.description: D5 sends the full manifest label set (`self-hosted`, `linux`, `ARM64`, `gx10`) as the `labels` field of `generate-jitconfig`, and spec scenario 'JIT labels match the routing labels' pins that equality. `self-hosted`, `Linux` and `ARM64` are runner-assigned default labels; GitHub's API documents `labels` as custom labels and may reject or silently dedupe the defaults (note also the case difference `linux` vs `Linux`, harmless for `runs-on` matching but visible in the runners list). Decide explicitly: either send only the custom labels (`gx10`) and have the test assert `manifest labels == defaults ∪ requested`, or record in O2/O6 that a 422 from `generate-jitconfig` on default labels is the expected failure signature and how to adapt.

Re-verification of open ledger item #5: partly resolved (the cache switch is now `$GX10_RUNNER_CACHE_ARGS` with word-splitting semantics specified and tested), but the remainder stands. D7's property list and test 3.1 still never name the `EnvironmentFile=%h/.config/gx10-runner/env` (or equivalent) line that must load `gx10-runner.env.example`'s values — without it `$GX10_RUNNER_CACHE_ARGS`, `--cpus`, `--memory`, the image ref and `GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED` are all unset in `ExecStart`/`ExecStartPre` — nor whether the credential reaches the mint script via `LoadCredential=github-token:<path>` or `GX10_RUNNER_TOKEN_FILE` (O2 stores it at `~ghrunner/.config/gx10-runner/token`, which matches neither statement). Pin both in D7 and assert them in 3.1.

Re-verification of open ledger items #19, #20, #21: all still open. The 'Runners Are Ephemeral Per Job' requirement text omits the `ExecStopPost` cleanup-runner.sh clause its own scenario checks; 'Runners Survive Host Reboot' does not require `install-units.sh` to be copy-and-print-only although its scenario does; and the tool-parity requirement does not acknowledge the D10 limit that indirect invocations via scripts are invisible to the scan and backstopped by O6. One sentence each closes them.

Re-verification of open ledger item #22: still open but acceptable as-is. The schema permits any label array while D3 hard-codes four labels; drift is caught by the test in task 2.1 (expression labels == manifest) and 3.3 (mint labels == manifest), so the manifest remains the source of truth and the schema stays reusable if labels change. Accept, or tighten with `minItems: 4` plus `contains` for `gx10` if a stronger static guarantee is wanted.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: reviewer recommends accept (same as #22)

items.description: Re-verification of open ledger item #23: still open. wp-runner-kit `outputs.artifacts` lists five files but omits `deploy/gx10-runner/gx10-runner.env.example`, `Containerfile`'s companion `toolchain.txt`, and the systemd unit's env example that tests 3.1 and D7 depend on. Add them so the integration package's scope check sees the full output set.

Re-verification of open ledger items #17 and #24: still present, accept. Pointing `contracts.openapi.primary` at the change-local README is this repository's recorded convention for changes with no HTTP surface, and change-local contract paths in work-packages.yaml are consumed only during the implementation phase, before archival; the path-stability rule targets tests. No action beyond the existing comment.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: reviewer itself recommends accept (same as #17/#24)

items.description: Re-verification of open ledger item #25: still open. A blank line separates A9 from A10/A11 in the proposal's assumptions list, splitting it into two Markdown lists. Remove the blank line. Also in tasks O4, the bullet 'Before enabling the units, install the host-service isolation control' is placed after the `systemctl --user enable --now` instruction; move it first so the runbook's step order matches its own wording.

Re-verification of open ledger item #26: unchanged. The two recorded degradations (coordinator projection forbidden at INIT, audit sink failure at the PLAN gate) are environment issues, not plan defects. Accept for this review; the orchestrator should confirm the audit sink is healthy before the IMPLEMENT phase records package decisions.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: environment degradations, not plan defects (duplicate of #26)

items.description: The runner unit remains underspecified and may be nonfunctional. D7 and task 3.1 do not require an EnvironmentFile entry that loads gx10-runner.env.example, while task 3.2 expects that file to supply the repository, image, limits, labels, retry budget, and cache arguments used by ExecStartPre and ExecStart. They also do not require LoadCredential=github-token:<path>, and the example environment-file task does not include GX10_RUNNER_TOKEN_FILE. An implementation can therefore satisfy every planned unit test while the mint script receives neither its configuration nor a credential. Specify both files unambiguously and test the EnvironmentFile and credential wiring.

The reboot/restart design still has no stale-container or stale-registration recovery. ExecStart uses a fixed container name without --replace, so a container retained after an unclean stop can make every subsequent restart fail with a name conflict. A hard reboot can also bypass ExecStopPost and leave an unused JIT registration offline indefinitely. Require tested pre-start cleanup or --replace for the container, and sweep offline registrations matching the instance's runner-name prefix before minting another registration.

wp-integration is declared responsible for merging the package branches, but its scope.write_allow permits writes only below openspec/changes/migrate-ci-to-self-hosted-gx10-runners/**. Merging wp-workflows, wp-runner-kit, wp-tooling, and wp-docs necessarily materializes changes under .github/, deploy/, scripts/, docs/, and skills/. Under scope enforcement the integration package cannot perform its declared work. Either make package materialization an explicit coordinator operation completed before wp-integration starts, or grant the integration package the exact output paths it must merge.

The requirement that the canonical expression's self-hosted labels equal routing.self_hosted_labels still lacks a scenario that changes the manifest independently and observes failure. The existing canonical-expression scenario can pass while repository_variable or dispatch_input in the manifest drifts from the hard-coded vars.CI_RUNNER_LANE and inputs.runner_lane references. Add a scenario and test tying all three routing fields to the expression.

The normative CLI contract for explicit run filters and bounded --limit fetching still has no behavioral scenario. Task 4.1 checks argument parsing only, so an implementation that accepts --limit but fetches every page before truncating can pass. Add a stubbed-gh scenario that asserts the emitted query filters and bounds the number of fetched results or pages.

D5 still claims that a job reading ACTIONS_RUNNER_INPUT_JITCONFIG gains nothing. The encoded JIT configuration contains runner identity and Actions-service credentials usable during the job's lifetime. Ephemerality limits the exposure but does not eliminate it. Document this residual capability accurately and either accept it explicitly or use an entrypoint that removes the value from the environment before executing job steps.

D8 says compare derives a run's lane from actual placement of its routed jobs but does not define the result when those jobs have mixed placement, no assigned runner, or conflicting labels. Such runs can otherwise be counted in either sample and distort the acceptance ratio. Define these runs as invalid or excluded with a diagnostic, and add a fixture covering mixed placement.

contracts.openapi.primary still names contracts/README.md even though that file is not an OpenAPI document. Schema validation based only on path existence can pass while consumers that parse the declared primary contract fail. Represent the absence of an OpenAPI surface using the work-package schema's supported sentinel or contract type; if the schema truly cannot express this, escalate that schema defect instead of publishing Markdown as OpenAPI.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: same as #24; work-package schema requires an openapi block; not a plan defect of this change

items.description: wp-runner-kit still omits deploy/gx10-runner/gx10-runner.env.example from outputs.artifacts even though the package authors it and the unit depends on its configuration contract. Add it to the declared outputs so package handoff and evidence collection include the required operator configuration.

The preferred host-service isolation control (D6, O4) is an nftables ruleset installed ad hoc as root, but nothing in D6, O4, O10 or the spec requires it to be persisted (/etc/nftables.conf + nftables.service, or a ufw/firewalld-managed rule) or re-verified after reboot. O10 verifies only that the runner units come back after `systemctl reboot`; the units will come back and immediately run PR code while the drop rule is gone, and a later ufw/firewalld reload can also flush a hand-added table. Require persistence in D6/O4, and extend O10's verification to re-run the O4 TCP-connect probes (or at least `nft list ruleset | grep skuid`) after the reboot.

O4's DNS check (`sudo -u ghrunner getent hosts api.github.com`, mirrored in the spec scenario 'ghrunner can still resolve api.github.com') does not exercise the path the nftables exemption protects. On Ubuntu 24.04 nsswitch uses `resolve [!UNAVAIL=return]`, so glibc getaddrinfo (getent and the mint script's curl alike) talks to systemd-resolved over the varlink/D-Bus unix socket and never sends UDP to 127.0.0.53. The check therefore passes even when the `ip daddr 127.0.0.53 udp dport 53 accept` rule is missing or ordered after the drop. The traffic that does hit 127.0.0.53 over UDP is slirp4netns forwarding container DNS (10.0.2.3), which this check never touches: a wrongly ordered rule leaves every runner unable to resolve github.com while O4 reports success. Probe from inside the container (`podman exec gx10-runner-1 getent hosts api.github.com`) and note that newer systemd also listens on 127.0.0.54, which the exemption should cover.

The D6 drop rule `fib daddr type local` blocks only the host's own addresses. slirp4netns NATs container traffic out through every host interface as `ghrunner`, including `tailscale0` and the LAN, so PR code on the GX10 can reach every tailnet peer and LAN host the operator's machine can (other machines' coordinator/Postgres instances, NAS, dev boxes), a lateral-movement surface the hosted lane never had. The design and A11 scope the isolation claim to 'host services' without stating that LAN/tailnet peers remain reachable. Either add `meta skuid ghrunner oifname "tailscale0" drop` plus a drop for RFC1918/CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) destinations, or record the residual explicitly as an accepted risk in A11 and the Risks table.

D6 and O4 give the nftables rules but never the table family. An operator who follows the text literally with `table ip` leaves IPv6 unfiltered: `fib daddr type local` in an `ip` table never sees `::1`, the host's link-local or ULA addresses, and the Tailscale IPv6 address, so a service bound to `[::]:54322` or `::1` stays reachable. The DNS exemption likewise only names an IPv4 stub. Pin `table inet` (and the `ip6 daddr ::1` exemption if resolved listens there) in D6, O4 and the spec scenario, and have the O4 probe loop include the host's IPv6 addresses from `hostname -I`.

Three SHALL clauses still have no WHEN/THEN. (1) 'Runners Are Ephemeral Per Job' requires `--replace` and `ExecStopPost runs cleanup-runner.sh`, but the only unit scenario ('Unit runs a removable container with a single-use config') asserts neither; ledger #19/#34 were closed by adding the requirement text, while the scenario the ledger assumed already checked ExecStopPost does not. (2) The verify_run clause 'every manifest job missing from the run' has no scenario; task 4.1 tests it but the spec does not. Task 3.1 and 4.1 cover both, so this is spec-only drift.

Ledger #8 is recorded as addressed, but the spec still gives `median_wallclock(runs)` and positional `compare(baseline, candidate, threshold=0.85, min_n=5)` while D8 defines keyword-only signatures with a `conclusion="success"` parameter on `median_wallclock`. Spec and design are both cited as contracts by task 4.1/4.2; the implementer has to pick one.

Task 2.8 says 'Test 2.4 asserts it [cache-local-path: /home/runner/.cache/uv] for routed jobs', but task 2.4's bullet list contains no such assertion and no spec scenario covers the setup-uv binding that the ledger #29 fix introduced in D6. Since 2.4 is written before 2.8 and is the RED test for it, the omission means the binding can be forgotten without any test failing, which is the exact failure mode #29 described.

wp-docs depends only on wp-contracts and runs in an isolated worktree in parallel with wp-runner-kit and wp-tooling, yet the runbook it writes is a contract over their outputs: script names, `GX10_RUNNER_CACHE_ARGS`, `GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED`, the env/token paths, the ci_wallclock flags. test_runbook.py (task 5.1) checks only O1..O12 headings, fenced blocks and two literal commands, and wp-integration adds no cross-check, so a variable renamed during implementation (as happened in planning with GX10_RUNNER_UV_CACHE) ships with a stale runbook that passes every gate. Either sequence wp-docs after wp-runner-kit/wp-tooling, or add an integration assertion that every `GX10_*` variable and `deploy/gx10-runner/*.sh` path named in the runbook exists in the kit and env example.

Because `compare` derives each run's lane from its jobs' runner labels, the CLI must issue one `actions/runs/<id>/jobs` GET per candidate run on top of the paginated runs listing. With the default `--limit 200` on each side that is up to ~400 extra requests per comparison against a 5000/hour PAT budget, and the mixed-placement exclusion rule means it cannot sample. D8 should state this cost and either default `--limit` lower for `compare`, or add `--jobs-concurrency`/caching of per-run lane results, so the O8 measurement does not stall on rate limiting.

Pass 3 records the pi lane as `auth_required` because pi wrote its findings to a file rather than stdout. That is pi's normal behaviour (it writes review_findings.json to the dispatcher's cwd), not an auth failure, so the lane's round-1 pass-3 findings were probably produced and discarded, and pi is now excluded from later rounds on a misclassification. Not a plan defect; the dispatcher's lane classifier should distinguish 'findings written to file' from auth failure, and the orchestrator may want to pick up the file before the next round.
items.resolution: orchestrator adjudication: dispatcher lane-classification issue, not a plan defect; reported to orchestrator

items.description: The fork-safety guarantee is implemented inside `ci.yml` and `security.yml`, but a `pull_request` run evaluates workflow YAML from the pull request's merge ref. A fork can therefore modify an existing workflow to replace the canonical `runs-on` expression with the public GX10 labels and remove the first-step guard; after the required external-contributor approval, that untrusted workflow can schedule directly on the repository-scoped runner. Tests cannot prevent this because runner selection occurs before any test or guard executes. The plan must not route `pull_request` or `merge_group` events to repository-scoped self-hosted runners unless enforcement is outside pull-request-controlled workflow YAML; the safe baseline is self-hosting only trusted `push` and suitably constrained `workflow_dispatch` runs.

D6 and O4 do not require the nftables isolation rules to be persisted across reboot, while lingering user units restart automatically at boot. O10 verifies only that the unit and runner return online, so a runtime-only nft rule can disappear during the reboot drill and expose LAN/Tailscale-bound host services as soon as the runners restart. Require persistent nftables configuration and extend O10 to recheck the rules, DNS exemption, and container TCP probes after reboot; the loopback-binding fallback must likewise be verified after reboot.

Operator step O1 assigns the fixed subordinate-ID ranges `200000-265535` without first proving they are unused in `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid`. Overlapping subordinate ranges can break rootless Podman isolation and allow different users' remapped container processes to share host IDs. The runbook should allocate a non-overlapping 65536-ID range using the host's account-management policy and verify that the resulting ranges do not overlap any existing entry.

D5 says the pre-mint sweep deletes every stale offline registration for an instance, but it performs only a runners-list request bounded to `per_page=100`. Once the repository has more than 100 registrations, a matching stale runner can fall outside that page and remain indefinitely; repeated hard reboots can accumulate registrations until runner creation or administration becomes unreliable. Specify bounded pagination across all available pages, or fail with an actionable diagnostic when the safety bound is reached, and test a match appearing after the first page.

The `Runners Are Ephemeral Per Job` requirement contains SHALL clauses that are not covered by a WHEN/THEN scenario as required by the review rules. In particular, no scenario asserts that `ExecStart` contains `--replace`, and no scenario asserts that `ExecStopPost` invokes `cleanup-runner.sh`; the current unit scenario checks neither despite tasks 3.1 planning both assertions. Add these outcomes to the unit scenario or create dedicated scenarios so the normative restart and cleanup contracts are represented in the spec itself.

fetch_runs changes per_page between pages, which breaks GitHub's page*per_page offset arithmetic. With --limit 150 it requests page=1&per_page=100 (runs 1-100) and then page=2&per_page=50, which GitHub serves as runs 51-100: the second half is duplicated and runs 101-150 are never fetched. Any --limit that is not a multiple of 100 and exceeds 100 silently double-counts runs in `median` and `compare` (and `cmd_compare` fetches jobs for the duplicates too). Keep per_page fixed at 100 and truncate to --limit after the loop.

test_cli_median_pages_until_limit only asserts the count of collected runs and the number of requests. The gh stub reproduces GitHub's offset math ((page-1)*per : page*per), so under the current per_page bug it returns ids 1-100 then 51-100 and the test still passes with n == 150. The test does not fail when the behaviour it targets is broken. Make the stub expose ids in the output (or assert on the recorded per_page/page arguments) and assert that the 150 ids are distinct and contiguous.

main() catches only GhError. A missing --workflow-file or --manifest path (FileNotFoundError), a malformed YAML definition, a jobs-API entry without the expected keys, or a run payload without head_sha (KeyError) escapes as a raw traceback instead of the documented non-zero error exit. The CLI is operator-facing in O6-O12; a clean error message beats a traceback when the operator is mid-runbook.

The comment misdescribes why the test passes. The stub returns a single job `build` on ubuntu-latest for every run, so run_lane classifies every run as `hosted` (not mixed); the baseline sample gets all 12 runs and the candidate sample is empty, and compare fails for insufficient candidate samples. The assertion holds for a different reason than stated, which will mislead the next person who edits the fixture.

test_job_counts (25/3), test_hosted_jobs_use_literal_hosted_label (n == 5) and test_routing_expression's `seen == 23` hard-code job counts that duplicate what the set-equality test already enforces. The design's stated mechanism for concurrent changes is 'manifest completeness test fails until they are classified'; with these counts, a correctly classified new job still fails three tests and forces an edit to the test files. The counts add brittleness without adding detection.

test_routed_job_drift_is_detected only asserts that two different strings normalise to different strings; it never runs the comparison logic against a workflow with a drifted job. Likewise test_manifest_completeness.test_unclassified_job_is_reported deletes a manifest entry and asserts a set difference, without exercising the assertion in test_job_sets_match_manifest or its message. Neither test fails if the real check regresses. Factor the check into a helper (e.g. `drifted_jobs(manifest, workflows) -> list[str]`) and assert on its output for a mutated input.

commands_in treats only line start, `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `$(`, `sudo` and `env` as command position, matching D10. Common shell prefixes `if`, `!`, `time`, `exec`, `xargs`, `nohup`, and loop bodies after `do`/`then` are not stripped, so `if ! sudo -n true; then` or `xargs docker rmi` in a routed job's run: block is not flagged. This is inside the design's documented limit (O6 dry run is the backstop) but worth recording since the spec text calls the scan an enforcement test.

The runbook's own notation says every 'as ghrunner' command must be run as `sudo -u ghrunner XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u ghrunner) <command>`, yet O3, O4 (install-units.sh, podman exec/inspect) and O9 (podman ps) use plain `sudo -u ghrunner podman ...`. Rootless podman resolves the runtime dir without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR only when /run/user/<uid> already exists, so O3 (run before linger has created a session in some orderings) can fall back to /tmp/podman-run-<uid> and build into a different storage than the units use. Separately, `deploy/gx10-runner` and `install-units.sh` are relative paths inside the operator's checkout; on Ubuntu 24.04 home directories are 0750, so ghrunner cannot read them and both commands fail with EACCES. The runbook should copy the kit to a world-readable location (e.g. /opt/gx10-runner-kit or ~ghrunner) before O3.

`systemctl enable --now nftables` starts the service only if it is inactive. On a host where nftables.service is already active (common when ufw or a previous ruleset is in use), the newly included file is not loaded, and the units enabled in the very next command start running PR code before the isolation rules exist. The O4 verify step would catch it afterwards, but the instruction should load the rules deterministically before the units are enabled.

tasks.md O4 (and the spec scenario 'Operator verifies host services are unreachable on every host address', which says the rules are 'present in /etc/nftables.conf') verify persistence with `grep -c skuid /etc/nftables.conf`. The runbook puts the rules in /etc/nftables.d/gx10-runner.nft and only an `include` line in /etc/nftables.conf, so that grep returns 0 on a correctly configured host. The runbook's own verify greps the include and the included file; the task and spec text should match it.

Task 2.9 is unchecked while the Status block marks Implementation complete and 6.1 (which depends on 2.9) is checked. The diff does include the edits 2.9 calls for (test_gate.py and test_ci_sweep_wiring.py were adjusted), so the box is stale rather than the work missing; but a goal gate reading tasks.md sees an incomplete phase.

The sudo removal only deletes NOPASSWD lines from /etc/sudoers; the `runner` user remains in the `sudo` group, the sudo binary stays installed, and /etc/sudoers.d/ is untouched. Today the upstream image writes its grant into /etc/sudoers itself, so this works, and --cap-drop ALL plus no-new-privileges make setuid sudo inert at runtime. It is fragile against an upstream move to /etc/sudoers.d/, and test_runner_image only checks that no grant is added, not that the inherited one is removed.

scripts/ci/ci_wallclock.py classifies a job as self-hosted only when its labels contain "gx10". A job on any other self-hosted runner will therefore be classified as hosted, allowing verify-run and the rollback check to approve hosted-pinned jobs that did not run on GitHub-hosted infrastructure and potentially contaminating comparison samples. Detect the standard "self-hosted" label separately, then require "gx10" when the expected lane is the GX10 lane.

mint-jitconfig.sh deletes matching runners while paginating the runners collection. Deleting entries from page 1 can shift entries formerly on page 2 onto page 1, causing the subsequent page-2 request to skip them. This violates the requirement to sweep every matching stale registration, and the fixed-page curl stub does not expose the defect. Collect matching IDs from all pages before deleting them, or repeatedly scan without page-shift gaps, and add a mutation-aware pagination test.

The Containerfile does not establish its claimed invariant that the runner user has no sudo grant. It removes NOPASSWD lines only from /etc/sudoers, silently ignores failures, and leaves grants under /etc/sudoers.d intact. test_runner_image.py additionally asserts that "sudoers.d" is absent from the Containerfile, preventing the straightforward hardening fix. Remove or disable applicable grants in both locations and verify the built image cannot execute sudo non-interactively.

install-units.sh prints bare `systemctl --user` commands after it returns to the invoking operator. If those commands are copied from a normal administrator shell, they target that administrator's user manager rather than the dedicated, nologin ghrunner account. Print complete commands using `sudo -u ghrunner XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u ghrunner) systemctl --user ...` (or the documented `--machine=ghrunner@` form) and update the tests to require the correct user context.

tasks.md task 2.9 explicitly says existing workflow-parsing test contracts must not be edited, but this change modifies both skills/tests/project-context-refresh/test_gate.py and skills/tests/validate-feature/test_ci_sweep_wiring.py. Since the new trigger and guard intentionally require these compatibility updates, revise the task contract to authorize and describe them rather than leaving the completed implementation in direct conflict with its approved plan.

mint-jitconfig.sh exits 1 immediately on any non-retryable HTTP status (401/403/404/422 — e.g. an expired or revoked 90-day PAT, a renamed repo, a deleted runner group). The unit runs with Restart=always, RestartSec=10 and StartLimitIntervalSec=0, so ExecStartPre is re-run every ~10 s on every instance indefinitely: with 8 instances that is ~48 generate-jitconfig POSTs per minute against the GitHub API with no back-off and no stopping condition. The unit comment promises 'back-off on persistent API failure', but the GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED backoff only covers 5xx/429/000; the non-retryable branch is the one that will fire during a credential outage. Fix: on a non-retryable code, sleep for a long bounded interval (e.g. min(GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED, 600)) before exiting, or write a sentinel the unit's ExecCondition honours, so a dead token degrades to a slow poll rather than a hot loop.

Runbook O4 writes the nftables ruleset with `sudo tee /etc/nftables.d/gx10-runner.nft` and later includes it from /etc/nftables.conf. Neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships an /etc/nftables.d/ directory (the stock nftables.conf has no include line and no drop-in dir), so on a fresh GX10 host `tee` fails with 'No such file or directory' and the operator continues to the `nft -f` step with no file. The step needs `sudo mkdir -p /etc/nftables.d` first, and the test for the runbook should assert that mkdir precedes tee.

Runbook O4 runs `sudo systemctl enable --now nftables` after loading the ruleset with `nft -f`. On Ubuntu the nftables service is installed but inactive by default; `--now` therefore starts it, which executes /etc/nftables.conf whose first statement in the stock file is `flush ruleset`. That wipes every table on the host — including podman's netavark/CNI tables and ufw's — and then reloads only what the conf includes. The runbook warns only against `systemctl restart nftables`; the `--now` on enable has the identical effect on a host where the service was not already running. Use `sudo systemctl enable nftables` (no --now) after the explicit `nft -f`, and tell the operator to verify `nft list ruleset | grep -c table` is unchanged afterwards.

gx10-runner@.service passes `--cpus ${GX10_RUNNER_CPUS}` to a rootless `podman run`. Rootless cgroup v2 limits require the `cpu` controller to be delegated to the user's `user@<uid>.service`; systemd's default delegation for user sessions is `memory pids` (plus `cpuset io cpu` only on newer distros when configured), so on a stock Ubuntu host every container start fails with 'requested cgroup controller `cpu` is not available' and, combined with Restart=always, the eight instances enter an infinite 10 s restart loop before a single job runs. The runbook O1 (ghrunner setup) must install a `/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf` drop-in with `[Service]\nDelegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids`, run daemon-reload, and O4 should verify `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-$(id -u ghrunner).slice/user@$(id -u ghrunner).service/cgroup.controllers` lists `cpu`.

tasks.md step O9 still instructs `journalctl --user -u gx10-runner@1 | grep -c 'Listening for Jobs'`. The runbook replaced this with `sudo journalctl _UID=$(id -u ghrunner) --user-unit gx10-runner@1.service` because the operator is not the ghrunner user and `--user` reads the caller's own journal; the runbook test forbids the old form. The task list and runbook now disagree on the verification command, so an operator following tasks.md gets an empty count and a false failure.

gx10-runner@.service declares `After=network-online.target` / `Wants=network-online.target`. Inside the user manager (systemd --user) there is no network-online.target with system semantics; the user instance has no NetworkManager-wait-online / systemd-networkd-wait-online job, so the target activates immediately and the ordering is a no-op. The mint script's retry/backoff already absorbs a not-yet-routable boot window, so this is informational: either remove the lines or add a comment that the real boot gate is the mint backoff, so a future reader does not rely on the directive.

In ci_wallclock.compare(), a run whose routed jobs executed on a non-GX10 self-hosted pool (job_lane returns OTHER_SELF_HOSTED) is silently dropped from both the hosted and the self-hosted sample: select() only records an exclusion when the lane is None or when the run belongs to the other side, and in the CLI path cmd_compare passes the same list as both sides, so the 'wrong lane' branch can never fire. An operator comparing during a partial cutover (or with a stray org-level runner picking up jobs) sees n shrink with nothing in excluded_runs to explain why, and can misread a thin sample as a scheduling problem. Record OTHER_SELF_HOSTED runs in excluded_runs with a reason.

The O4 nftables persistence procedure can erase the host's existing firewall rules. The runbook appends the runner table to `/etc/nftables.conf`, whose stock configuration may contain `flush ruleset`, and then enables `nftables.service`. Although the text correctly warns that restarting the service would replay the flush, `systemctl enable --now nftables` does exactly that when the service is inactive, and the same flush occurs at boot. This can wipe UFW/firewalld or other host rules before recreating only the GX10 table. Persist the runner table through a dedicated ordered unit or integrate it with the host's authoritative firewall manager without replaying a global flush.

`verify_run` silently accepts a successful non-skipped job when the jobs API entry has no runner labels. Both hosted and routed placement checks are conditional on `actual is not None`, so missing placement evidence produces no violation. This contradicts the requirement to report every routed job that did not run on a `gx10`-labelled runner and can let O6/O7/O12 report zero violations without proving placement. Treat an unassigned/unknown lane on every non-skipped job as a placement violation and add tests for both expected lanes and hosted-pinned jobs.

`GX10_RUNNER_CACHE_ARGS` is expanded as unrestricted Podman arguments after the hardening flags, but nothing enforces the documented single allowed value. A configured value such as `--network host`, `--privileged`, `--cap-add ALL`, or an arbitrary bind mount can override or defeat the unit's isolation; the tests only exercise the empty and expected named-volume values and therefore do not detect this. Replace the free-form argument variable with a validated boolean/fixed wrapper or reject every value except empty and the exact documented volume pair before `ExecStart`.

Three tests pin the lane census to literal counts: test_manifest_completeness.test_job_counts asserts 25 ci.yml / 3 security.yml jobs and test_hosted_jobs_use_literal_hosted_label asserts exactly 5 hosted jobs; test_routing_expression.test_every_routed_job_uses_canonical_expression asserts exactly 23 routed jobs. The set-equality checks already catch unclassified and stale entries, so these counts add no protection, but they turn every legitimate manifest move (the O6 `amd64-only` move, an O8 `measured-slower` move, any new job added by a concurrent change) into a mandatory test edit — contradicting D2/D8's promise that reclassification is a manifest-only change. Drop the literal counts or derive them from the manifest.

commands_in() stops scanning a segment at the first non-watched word, so a disallowed command that follows a shell keyword or wrapper is never seen: `if test -f x; then docker build .; fi`, `for f in *; do podman load < $f; done`, `time docker run`, `exec sudo ...`, `timeout 60 apt-get ...`, `xargs docker rm`. Only `sudo` and `env` are treated as pass-through prefixes. This matches the letter of D10 but a routed job can be written (even accidentally) to call a container engine in a form the gate misses, and the O6 dry run is then the only backstop. Extend the pass-through set with at least then/do/else/elif/time/exec/timeout/nohup/xargs (and `!`).

test_runbook_uses_only_flags_the_cli_accepts captures `ci_wallclock.py <cmd>([^\n`]*)`, so flags on a backslash-continued line are never checked. The O8 `compare` invocation puts `--workflow`, `--event` and `--head-sha` on the continuation line and the two `median` invocations put `--since`/`--until`/`--limit` there too; a typo in any of those would pass this test. Join `\\\n` continuations before matching.

The mint budget clock (`start_us`) starts after the sweep, but TimeoutStartSec=900 bounds the whole ExecStartPre. Sweep worst case is 10 listing GETs plus N DELETEs, each with `--max-time 30`; a slow-but-responding API (not an outage, which fails fast with 000 on page 1) can spend several minutes there, after which the full 600 s mint budget (plus up to 30 s of in-flight request) can push past 900 s. systemd then kills the script mid-backoff and restarts every RestartSec=10 — the exact hammering D5 sets out to avoid. Start the budget clock before the sweep, or cap sweep time against the same budget.

compare() indexes `r["id"]` in lane_of/select while the sibling code uses `r.get("id")`, and _workflow_jobs() assumes the parsed workflow is a mapping; a run without an `id`, or a workflow fetched at head_sha that parses to a list/scalar (e.g. a stub or a non-workflow file at that ref), raises KeyError/AttributeError. KeyError is caught by main(), AttributeError is not, so the CLI would print a traceback instead of the `error:` line the test test_cli_reports_bad_input_files_without_traceback promises. Guard the definition shape (`isinstance(..., dict)`) and use consistent id access.

The unit runs `podman run` in the foreground under `Type=simple`. Podman's documented systemd integration (and `podman generate systemd`/Quadlet) uses `Type=notify` with `--sdnotify=conmon` so the unit is only `active` once the container is actually running, and `--cgroups=split` so the container's processes stay inside the service cgroup for `systemctl stop`/KillMode. With `simple`, O10's `is-active gx10-runner@1` can report `active` while the container is still being created, and a container whose conmon landed in a sibling cgroup may outlive the unit's SIGKILL (mitigated here by `--rm --replace`). Acceptable for an 8-instance pool; recorded so a future unit change picks the notify form deliberately.

Requirement 'Routed Jobs Default To The Hosted Lane' states the expression resolves to ubuntu-latest for 'never any other event', but no scenario exercises an event outside {push, pull_request, merge_group, workflow_dispatch}. The test table covers `schedule` and the fork-guard test covers `pull_request_target`, so the behaviour is pinned in code but the normative text has no WHEN/THEN for it. Add a scenario (e.g. a `schedule` event with CI_RUNNER_LANE=self-hosted resolves to ubuntu-latest).

`install-units.sh -h` prints header lines 2-9, which document `--prefix` only; `--instances N` (and the `GX10_INSTANCES` env fallback) are accepted but undocumented in the help text and the header comment.

The claimed start-time bound is incorrect. `mint-jitconfig.sh` starts its 600-second retry clock only after the stale-runner sweep, which may make 10 sequential API calls at up to 30 seconds each. A final mint request may also run for 30 seconds after the budget is effectively exhausted. The resulting worst case exceeds 930 seconds, while `gx10-runner@.service` sets `TimeoutStartSec=900`. systemd can therefore terminate `ExecStartPre` mid-operation. The test only compares 600 against 900 and misses the sweep and request overhead. Include all API work in one budget or increase the timeout with margin and test the composite bound.

The host-side scripts require `curl` and `jq`, but the runbook never installs or verifies those host prerequisites. Adding them to the runner container's `toolchain.txt` does not help `ExecStartPre` or `ExecStopPost`, which execute on the host. A valid Ubuntu/Podman installation may therefore enter a restart loop immediately because `jq` or `curl` is absent. Add an operator prerequisite/install step and verification before enabling the units.

`ci_wallclock.py` does not handle structurally invalid but syntactically valid YAML inputs. For example, a `--workflow-file` containing a YAML list reaches `_workflow_jobs()` and raises an uncaught `AttributeError`; malformed manifest shapes similarly raise uncaught `TypeError` or `AttributeError`. `main()` does not catch these exceptions, so the operator gets a traceback instead of the documented controlled error exit. Validate loaded document types or catch and translate these failures, and add a test using valid YAML with the wrong structure.

validation-report.md classifies the 12 full-suite failures (multiplayer-simulation, roadmap-runtime) as pre-existing and unrelated, but the report itself states 'No baseline full-suite run on main was made'. I checked the plausible interference mechanisms and found none: skills/tests/ci_runners is a proper package (__init__.py), none of its test basenames collide with the duplicate basenames that already exist across other suites (test_cli.py, test_models.py, etc. are all pre-existing), the only sys.modules keys it registers are the unique 'ci_wallclock' and 'ci_wallclock_rb', conftest fixtures are package-scoped, and skills/pyproject.toml only appends tests/ci_runners to testpaths. The 'unrelated' claim is therefore well-supported by reasoning, but the report presents it as established rather than inferred. Suggest one sentence noting the claim rests on the isolation control run (477 passed) plus absence of shared state, not on a main baseline. Note: I could not independently re-run the ci_runners suite in this review (command denied by the permission system); the 202-pass figure is taken from the report.

tasks.md Status checklist still shows '- [ ] Testing' and '- [ ] Review' while validation-report.md records VALIDATE pass with 199 ci_runners tests green and IMPL_REVIEW converged over three rounds. The change artefacts disagree about phase state; the goal gate and archive tooling read tasks.md.

IMPL_REVIEW round-3 unlabelled-job check verified: verify_run in scripts/ci/ci_wallclock.py reports a placement violation ('placement is unproven') when job_lane(entry) is None for a non-skipped job, and test_job_that_ran_without_labels_is_a_placement_violation pins it across both lanes and two job names. However compare()'s run_lane helper silently drops unlabelled jobs, and a run whose routed jobs are all unlabelled is excluded as 'no routed job was assigned a runner'. The two entry points therefore treat the same data differently: verify-run fails loudly, compare quietly shrinks the sample. This is acceptable because compare is a measurement tool and verify-run is the enforcement point (O8 vs O6/O9 in the runbook), but the median can be computed over fewer runs than the operator believes without any warning.

Placement evidence relies on the Jobs API `labels` field, which echoes the labels the job requested, not the runner that executed it. For self-hosted lanes this is sufficient (GitHub only assigns runners holding all requested labels). For the hosted lane, a rogue self-hosted runner registered with the label `ubuntu-latest` would satisfy the requested labels while actually being self-hosted; the OTHER_SELF_HOSTED check only catches runners that advertise `self-hosted`. runner_name / runner_id (also in the Jobs API payload) identify the actual machine and would close that gap. This is a hardening observation, not a defect in the stated acceptance criteria.

Re-verification of ledger [106] (single mint time budget vs TimeoutStartSec). Mechanics are correct: start_us is captured before sweep(), fits() refuses any request whose delay+req_max would overrun GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED (600), the sweep is capped at budget/2, and the fail_slow hold-off (300) is clipped to the remaining budget, so worst-case ExecStartPre is bounded well under TimeoutStartSec=900. Tests pin it: test_whole_mint_run_is_bounded_below_the_start_timeout asserts max_elapsed + req_max < timeout and holdoff <= max_elapsed; test_no_request_starts_when_it_cannot_finish_inside_the_budget proves zero curl calls when REQ_MAX exceeds the budget; test_hold_off_is_clipped_to_the_remaining_budget covers the clip. One wording inaccuracy only: the ledger text says the tests 'drive the curl stub with slow responses'; they do not. The bound is pinned by static analysis of the script plus the REQ_MAX>budget trick, not by a slow-responding stub. The ledger entry should be reworded, no code change needed.

IMPL_REVIEW round-3 isolation unit verified: the dedicated oneshot gx10-runner-isolation.service (DefaultDependencies=no, Before=network-pre.target systemd-user-sessions.service) loads an idempotent `table inet gx10_runner_isolation` whose DNS exemption to 127.0.0.53 precedes `fib daddr type local drop`, and never routes through nftables.service (whose config begins with `flush ruleset`). test_nft_ruleset_is_ordered_persistent_and_dual_stack pins the rule ordering, the ExecStart line, the Before= ordering, the absence of `flush ruleset` and bans `enable --now nftables`. One gap: the unit has no ExecStop that deletes the table, so `systemctl stop gx10-runner-isolation` leaves the drop rules live. That is the safe failure direction for a code-execution surface and the runbook's O12 rollback does not depend on it, so this is informational.

D10 says routed jobs pin tool setup actions to 'the same major version the repository uses elsewhere'. The only actions/setup-node pin in .github/workflows is the new one at ci.yml:391 (@v6), so the rule is vacuously satisfied and there is no existing major to agree with. Not a defect; noting so a future reviewer does not look for a mismatch.

The dedicated nftables boot unit does not guarantee that isolation is active before the lingering runner user manager starts. It is ordered before `systemd-user-sessions.service`, but systemd v255's `user@.service` has no ordering dependency on that service; `enable-linger` starts the user manager at boot independently. Moreover, `Before=` supplies ordering only, so an nft load failure would not prevent the runner units from starting. This leaves a boot-time path for PR code to run without host-network isolation. `test_nft_ruleset_is_ordered_persistent_and_dual_stack` merely pins the insufficient `Before=network-pre.target systemd-user-sessions.service` text and does not test the resolved dependency graph or failure behavior. Establish a hard ordering and failure dependency between the isolation service and the actual lingering user manager/runner startup, then test that relationship.

The mint script's claimed single total time budget is not enforced for sweep API calls. `sweep()` calls `api_call` after checking only its half-budget elapsed cap, without checking that the request's `GX10_MINT_REQ_MAX` fits in the remaining overall budget. For example, `GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED=10` with the default 30-second request maximum can exceed the advertised 10-second total on the first sweep request. The round-3 test claims every request is budget-checked but only searches globally for `if ! fits 0`; that check belongs to the later mint loop and does not pin sweep behavior. Check `fits` before every API request or validate the budget/request relationship, and add a timed stub regression covering sweep plus mint/hold-off under one budget.

Pending-operator observation, not a defect. The nftables ruleset exempts only 127.0.0.53 for DNS before dropping all private, CGNAT and link-local destinations. The container runs with slirp4netns:allow_host_loopback=false, so rootless podman will not hand the container the host's 127.0.0.53 stub; podman instead copies the upstream servers from /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf (or /etc/resolv.conf). If the GX10 host's upstream resolver is a LAN router (192.168.x.x) or the Tailscale MagicDNS address (100.100.100.100), those addresses fall inside the dropped ranges and in-container DNS fails, which would surface as every job failing to reach api.github.com. The runbook's O4 in-container 'getent hosts api.github.com' check is exactly the probe that catches this, and the fix (a public upstream resolver for the ghrunner user, or an explicit --dns on the podman run line) is an operator choice. Suggest the runbook name this cause next to O4 so the first failure is diagnosable without a network trace.
